identification.summary: Cyber Serp (CyberSerp) is a Telegram-based group that claimed responsibility for a March 2026 phishing campaign impersonating CERT-UA to deliver the Go-based AGEWHEEZE remote access trojan to Ukrainian recipients; CERT-UA tracks the activity as UAC-0255 under CERT-UA#21075 [S1][S2][S3][S4]. CERT-UA linked UAC-0255 to the CyberSerp Telegram channel, which publicly claimed the attack on 2026-03-28 [S1][S2]. The group presents itself as a Ukrainian collective, while a Russian-language comment was reportedly found in the fake site's HTML [S5].
identification.notes: Only one campaign is publicly documented in the sources reviewed [S1][S4]. Name variants: Cyber Serp, CyberSerp, UAC-0255 (CERT-UA identifier) [S1][S2]. No Microsoft name identified.

attribution.basis: CERT-UA tied UAC-0255 to the CyberSerp Telegram channel, and the fake domain's HTML contained a Russian-language comment naming CYBER SERP, per Bitdefender [S1][S4]. The group describes itself as Ukrainian, but the Russian-language comment is cited as the main reason to suspect otherwise [S5][S4]. No source reviewed states state sponsorship or a government attribution.

objectives: Stated or implied objective is remote access to victim endpoints in Ukraine via the AGEWHEEZE RAT; the underlying motive (espionage, disruption, notoriety) is not established in the sources reviewed [S1][S3]. Public Telegram claim of the attack suggests a notoriety element [S2][S4].

targeting.notes: Targeted victims included Ukrainian government agencies, healthcare, financial and educational organizations [S3]. CERT-UA reported only a few infections, mainly personal devices of educational institution employees [S4][S2]. A claim of about 1 million recipients circulated via Telegram and one vendor blog; treat as unverified [S4][S6].

capabilities.summary: Delivery was by emails impersonating CERT-UA (e.g., from incidents@cert-ua.tech) sent 2026-03-26 and 2026-03-27, with a password-protected ZIP (CERT_UA_protection_tool.zip) hosted on Files.fm presented as security software [S4][S3]. The payload, AGEWHEEZE, is a Go RAT communicating over WebSockets (reported C2 at an OVH-hosted IP on port 8443 with a self-signed certificate) that supports command execution, file operations, clipboard monitoring, keyboard and mouse emulation, screenshots, and process/service management [S3][S4]. Persistence is via scheduled tasks (reported names SvcHelper and CoreService), registry Run keys, or Startup entries [S3][S4]. The lookalike site was likely AI-generated [S4].

campaigns.name: CERT-UA impersonation / AGEWHEEZE phishing (CERT-UA#21075)
campaigns.summary: Phishing emails impersonating CERT-UA were sent 2026-03-26 and 2026-03-27 delivering a password-protected ZIP with the AGEWHEEZE RAT [S4][S3]. The CyberSerp Telegram channel claimed the attack on 2026-03-28 [S2]. CERT-UA assessed few infections, mostly personal devices of education-sector staff [S4][S2].

diamond.adversary: Cyber Serp / UAC-0255, a Telegram-fronted group of unknown composition and location [S1][S5].
diamond.capability: Phishing with brand impersonation, Go-based AGEWHEEZE RAT with persistence mechanisms [S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Lookalike domain cert-ua.tech, Files.fm file hosting, OVH-hosted WebSocket C2 on port 8443, Telegram channel for claims [S3][S4][S2].
diamond.victim: Ukrainian public and private sector organizations; confirmed infections mainly education-sector personal devices [S3][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Activity occurs in the context of the Russia-Ukraine conflict and a trend of impersonating trusted Ukrainian entities (earlier UAC-0190, UAC-0252) [S2]; ideological alignment of the group is unconfirmed [S5].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints, email, and file-sharing services; Go malware over WebSockets [S3][S4].

gaps: Primary CERT-UA#21075 advisory could not be opened (fetch blocked); details rely on secondary coverage.
Group origin, membership, and any state link are unknown; self-described Ukrainian identity versus Russian-language artifact is unresolved.
Actual victim count and recipient volume unverified (1 million figure is unconfirmed).
Motive and prior or subsequent activity not found in sources reviewed.
Malpedia and MITRE entries not opened; no MITRE group ID known.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: the relevant environment is Ukrainian government, health, finance, and education email and endpoint space, where trusted-entity impersonation of CERT-UA erodes defender credibility [S3][S2]. Step 3: the actor shows low-to-moderate sophistication, with AI-assisted lure infrastructure and a commodity-style Go RAT [S4]. Step 4 MLCOA: further impersonation phishing with file-sharing-hosted archives against Ukrainian entities; MDCOA: broader volume campaigns or use of the access for follow-on operations (not evidenced). Candidate indicators: emails from lookalike cert-ua domains, Files.fm password-protected ZIPs, scheduled tasks SvcHelper/CoreService, outbound WebSocket to port 8443 on a self-signed host [S3][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track CERT-UA advisories and Telegram claims, treating actor claims of scale as unverified [S4]. Authorities: for non-Ukrainian partners, sharing and defensive actions fall under existing network defense authorities; no offensive implication drawn from sources. Mission assurance: verify the authenticity of any CERT or government security-tool email via out-of-band channels and block execution of password-protected archives. Coordination: relay IOCs to Ukrainian partners and CERT-UA via established channels [S2][S3].
